microtheory.name: motion_perception_visual
microtheory.definition: Perception of motion. Direction-selective cells, motion energy models, motion-induced illusions, biological motion, structure-from-motion. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal-change visual processing.

concepts.name: motion_selective_neuron_v1
concepts.definition: V1 + MT/V5 neurons preferentially responding to motion in specific direction. Substrate analogue: substrate's directional-temporal feature.

concepts.name: mt_v5
concepts.definition: Middle temporal area. Strongly motion-selective. Lesion → akinetopsia (motion blindness). Substrate analogue: substrate's specialized motion-processing Mt.

concepts.name: akinetopsia
concepts.definition: Motion blindness from MT damage. World appears as series of stills. Substrate analogue: substrate's motion-Mt failure mode.

concepts.name: directional_selectivity_visual
concepts.definition: Neuron responds preferentially to one motion direction. Tuned by leftward-rightward connections. Substrate analogue: substrate's direction-tuned concept.

concepts.name: apparent_motion
concepts.definition: Discrete stimuli at successive positions appear to move continuously. Phi phenomenon. Foundation of film + animation. Substrate analogue: substrate's interpolation-based motion.

concepts.name: aperture_problem
concepts.definition: Local motion detector can only see component perpendicular to edge. Ambiguous. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-vs-global motion ambiguity.

concepts.name: motion_aftereffect
concepts.definition: Adapt to motion → stationary appears to move opposite direction. Waterfall illusion. Substrate analogue: substrate's motion-channel adaptation.

concepts.name: induced_motion
concepts.definition: Stationary target appears to move when surround moves. Substrate analogue: substrate's reference-frame ambiguity.

concepts.name: global_motion_pooling
concepts.definition: Integrate local motion signals across area to estimate global direction. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial-pooling for motion.

concepts.name: motion_energy_model
concepts.definition: Adelson + Bergen 1985. Motion detection via space-time oriented filters. Substrate analogue: substrate's space-time feature detector.

concepts.name: reichardt_detector
concepts.definition: Classic motion detector — comparing delayed signal from one location with undelayed from another. Substrate analogue: substrate's delay-line motion detector.

concepts.name: optic_flow
concepts.definition: Pattern of motion across visual field from observer's movement. Gibson 1950. Cue to heading, structure, depth. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-motion-induced visual flow.

concepts.name: focus_of_expansion
concepts.definition: Point in optic flow that doesn't move during forward locomotion. Indicates heading. Substrate analogue: substrate's heading estimator.

concepts.name: vection
concepts.definition: Illusion of self-motion induced by visual flow. Substrate analogue: substrate's flow-based motion attribution.

concepts.name: biological_motion
concepts.definition: Perception of moving humans + animals from sparse cues. Johansson's point-light walkers. Recognized rapidly. Substrate analogue: substrate's specialized biomotion recognition.

concepts.name: point_light_walker
concepts.definition: Johansson 1973. Body marked by ~12 dots; only motion visible. Recognizable as walking human in <1s. Substrate analogue: substrate's compressed-motion recognition.

concepts.name: biological_motion_area
concepts.definition: STS (superior temporal sulcus) specialized for biomotion. Substrate analogue: substrate's specialized motion-category Mt.

concepts.name: structure_from_motion
concepts.definition: Recover 3D structure from 2D motion sequence. Tomasi + Kanade factorization. Substrate analogue: substrate's 3D-from-temporal-input reconstruction.

concepts.name: rigidity_assumption
concepts.definition: Prior assumption that scenes consist of rigid objects. Drives SFM. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural prior.

concepts.name: smooth_pursuit_motion
concepts.definition: Slow eye movement to track moving target. Up to ~100 deg/s. Substrate analogue: substrate's continuous-tracking attention.

concepts.name: optokinetic_nystagmus
concepts.definition: Reflex eye movement stabilizing image during head/world motion. Substrate analogue: substrate's image-stabilization reflex.

concepts.name: vestibulo_ocular_reflex
concepts.definition: Eye movement counteracting head movement, keeping gaze stable. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-motion compensation.

rules.name: aperture_problem_requires_global_pooling
rules.head: the substrate detects motion locally
rules.body: individual detectors are ambiguous (aperture problem); resolution requires pooling across spatial extent. Substrate's local-global motion integration.

rules.name: optic_flow_signals_self_motion
rules.head: the substrate moves through the world
rules.body: optic flow pattern signals direction + speed + structure. Focus of expansion = heading. Substrate's self-motion signal.

rules.name: biological_motion_recognized_from_sparse_cues
rules.head: the substrate sees minimal motion cues from human or animal
rules.body: specialized processing rapidly recognizes it as biological. Johansson 1973. Substrate's specialized biomotion.

rules.name: motion_aftereffect_reveals_adaptation
rules.head: the substrate adapts to sustained motion
rules.body: direction-selective channels fatigue; stationary input now activates opposite-direction channels — motion aftereffect. Substrate's channel-adaptation.

rules.name: rigidity_constrains_structure_from_motion
rules.head: the substrate recovers 3D from temporal sequence
rules.body: the rigidity assumption converts ambiguous 2D motion to unique 3D structure. Substrate's structural prior in SFM.
